clue.text: Revere, for example, a saint

definitions.meaning: ... Revere, the American patriot famed for his midnight ride of 1775, is one bearer of the name
the apostle of Tarsus, author of many New Testament epistles, is a saint

explanation.surface: A patriot of the American Revolution is offered up as an example of sainthood.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the patriot Revere and the name of the apostle saint are the same word.

clue.text: Representative of pontiff, say, coming in behind

indicators.note: coming in tells us the abbreviation for 'say' enters the word for behind

parts.note: behind, as in behind schedule, means late
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A papal envoy, as one might put it, is arriving at the back of the procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position but means LATE (behind time).
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an official envoy sent by the Pope to act on his behalf.

clue.text: Finally found skill in another arrangement

indicators.note: in places the word for skill within the word another before everything is rearranged
arrangement signals that the combined letters are reordered into a new phrase

parts.note: skill is art, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Artistic talent can be found within a fresh arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally found' looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition, a hunting idiom; 'in' and 'arrangement' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something to earth is an idiom from fox hunting meaning to track it down at last.

clue.text: Least productive learner that is put outside

indicators.note: put outside tells us the Latin for 'that is' wraps around the learner's letter

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is, the full form of ie
L is the learner, from the L-plates on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: The laziest student has been thrown out of the class, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: The idlest worker is the laziest, and so the one producing least.

clue.text: Protecting king, save comrade in violent fashion

indicators.note: Protecting means the word for save surrounds the letter for king like a guard

parts.note: save means except, which is but
R is short for rex, Latin for king
a comrade is an ally

explanation.surface: A bodyguard shielding the monarch rescues a friend with great ferocity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like a verb meaning rescue but is the preposition BUT (except).
explanation.definitionFit: Acting brutally means behaving with savage violence, an adverbial match.

clue.text: King jealous of his nobles, initially

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A monarch is suspicious and envious of the barons at his court.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the English King John, forced by his barons to seal Magna Carta in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: John was a king of England, and the name is also that of many popes.

clue.text: One jerk in game, who operates on right or left wing?

definitions.text: who operates on right or left wing?

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces for one and jerk sit within the name of the game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
I is the Roman numeral one
a tic is a sudden involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A player suffers a spasm during a match, playing on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wing' suggests a sports position, but here it is the political wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is a politician, someone who works on the political right or left.

clue.text: Fish, such as eleven named in this puzzle

definitions.meaning: the ruffe, a small freshwater perch, is also called by this name

definitions.text: such as eleven named in this puzzle
definitions.meaning: eleven of the other answers are names taken by bishops of Rome

explanation.surface: A fish is said to be one of the many in this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Popes are the theme: Paul, John, Alexander, Clement, Peter, Stephen and others are papal names; the ruffe is also a pope.

clue.text: Scottish king able to make a law as well as English king

parts.note: lex is Latin for law
as well as means and
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Scottish monarch can pass legislation as the English one does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'able to make' is a link saying the pieces produce the king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander I, II and III were medieval kings of Scotland; Alexander is also a papal name.

clue.text: Moulding seen in old book — short, with rounded shape

indicators.note: short means the word for book is cut down to its usual abbreviation

parts.note: a book is a volume
the letter O has a round shape

explanation.surface: An architectural moulding appears in an old, brief book with a curved form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims VOLUME to VOL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex moulding with a quarter-round profile, used in classical architecture.

clue.text: Listed answer in fast time

indicators.note: in places the letter for answer inside the period of fasting

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A recorded answer was given within a short time limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed' is not about lists: a ship that lists tilts to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that listed tilted over, so it leaned to one side.

clue.text: Exist, even though scattered over large area

indicators.note: scattered tells us the letters of the two words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Things can exist even though they are spread thinly across a wide region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges EXIST and EVEN; 'though' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extensive covers or reaches across a wide expanse.

clue.text: Extract from article men thought mild

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A passage from an essay shows that the men were gentle in their thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild, and a clement person is merciful; Clement is also a papal name.

clue.text: Holds one's own ecclesiastical garments

definitions.meaning: manages or deals successfully with a difficulty
long cloaks worn by priests in processions

explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage; copes are long semicircular cloaks worn by clergy.

clue.text: Like wild animal, one going crazy when held by rope

indicators.note: when held by places the scrambled word inside the word for rope

parts.note: a line is a rope, especially at sea

indicators.note: going crazy tells us the letters of the word one are jumbled

explanation.surface: An individual loses his mind while tied up with a cord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like wild animal' is vague on purpose: the beast is a lion, and the scrambled ONE gives EON.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, describing a big wild cat; Leo is also a papal name.

clue.text: Unobtrusively playing not just any old piano

parts.note: a show that is playing is on
the definite article picks out a particular thing rather than any one at all
piano is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A performer plays a piano that is genuinely special, but without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' looks like the instrument but is the musical marking for softly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the quiet means doing it secretly, without drawing attention.

clue.text: Head off upper-class people getting on stage

indicators.note: Head off means the first letter of the word for the upper classes is removed

parts.note: the gentry are people of good social position just below the nobility

explanation.surface: The aristocrats are stopped from making an appearance in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a verb meaning intercept but drops G from GENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's entry is the moment of walking onto the stage.

clue.text: Safe time to look around

indicators.note: around places the word for looking around the letter for time

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: It is a good moment to glance about you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like an adjective but is a noun: old criminal slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: In safecracking slang a peter is a safe or strongbox; Peter is also the first pope.

clue.text: Uplifting airs — they help maintain warm feelings

definitions.meaning: rising currents of warm air used by gliders and birds
warm underwear keeps the wearer cosy

explanation.definitionFit: Thermals are rising warm air currents, and also thermal underclothes.

clue.text: Name of female climber

definitions.meaning: an evergreen plant that climbs walls and trees

explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a woman's name and also the climbing plant.

clue.text: Child at home, without a penny?

parts.note: someone at home is in
without means having no
a cent is a penny in American usage

explanation.surface: A youngster stays indoors because there is no pocket money.
explanation.definitionFit: An innocent is a guileless person, such as a young child; Innocent is also a papal name.

clue.text: Fish left part of Thames by Waterloo?

indicators.note: left part of picks the leftmost letter, the first, of the river's name

parts.note: the battle of Waterloo was a rout for Napoleon, a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A fish deserted a stretch of the London river near Waterloo station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb but picks the leftmost letter; Waterloo is the battle, not the London station.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout is a freshwater fish in the salmon family.

clue.text: Male celebrated on Boxing Day, dancing with female

parts.note: a step is a dance movement, so dancing is stepping
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A man is partying on 26 December, dancing with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing Day (26 December, a British holiday) is the feast of St Stephen.
explanation.definitionFit: St Stephen, the first Christian martyr, has his feast day on 26 December; Stephen is also a papal name.

clue.text: Man from work unit returned covered in blood

indicators.note: returned means the word for a unit of work is read backwards

parts.note: an erg is a unit of work or energy in physics
gory means covered in blood

explanation.surface: A man from the factory came back bloodied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ERG into GRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregory is a man's given name, and also a papal name.

clue.text: Remarkable brain I found in taxonomic group

indicators.note: found in tells us the letter I sits within the classification word

parts.note: a genus is a rank in biological classification above species

explanation.surface: A scientist discovers he belongs in a particular biological category.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius is a person of exceptional intellect, a brilliant mind.

clue.text: Gold coins used in round-the-world trips

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
bits are small coins, as in a threepenny bit, an old British coin

explanation.surface: Gold coins are spent on journeys around the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbits are circuits around a body, such as spacecraft flights round the Earth.

clue.text: West Indian monk

definitions.meaning: a native of the Caribbean island of Dominica or the ... Republic
a member of the order of preachers founded by St Dominic

explanation.definitionFit: Dominican describes someone from Dominica, and also a friar of St Dominic's order.

clue.text: Remove from head office

indicators.note: from signals the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone is taken away from the company headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove from head' looks like the definition (as of a hat), but 'from' is the hidden-word signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To doff is to take off, especially a hat in greeting.

clue.text: Immediately succeeding, having caught ten?

indicators.note: having means the word for caught holds the letter for ten inside it

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it, so netted means caught
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Something follows straight on after a catch of ten fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means coming straight after in order or time.

clue.text: From a city, one in Africa (not capital)

indicators.note: not capital means the opening capital letter of the city's name is dropped

parts.note: Durban is a South African port city

explanation.surface: Someone comes from a city in Africa that is not the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not capital' seems to describe the city (Durban is no capital) but also drops its capital letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban means relating to a city or town; Urban is also a papal name.

clue.text: Signed agreement with European part of network

parts.note: a nod is a signal of agreement given by a gesture

explanation.surface: A European signs a deal to join a business network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signed' suggests a signature but means gestured: a nod.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a connection point in a network where lines meet.

clue.text: Turbulent life and times of Mendelssohn, for one

indicators.note: Turbulent says the letters of life are tossed into disorder

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: The composer Mendelssohn had a stormy life and era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turbulent' rearranges LIFE; 'times' is the multiplication sign, not an era.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix Mendelssohn was the German composer; Felix is also a papal name.

clue.text: Ate sundae that's contaminated, becoming this?

definitions.text: Ate sundae that's contaminated, becoming this?

indicators.note: contaminated says the letters of the two words are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone eats a tainted ice cream and is asked how it leaves them feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contaminated' rearranges ATE SUNDAE; the whole clue also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a tainted dessert would leave one queasy and sick to the stomach.
